messages:
anya: FYI onboarding magnet-32k-int4v2 hit a strange longprefill artifact. After a runtime autoshrink the decoder re-emits tokens from ~7k tokens earlier. Minimal repro + logs below. Anyone have ideas?

ben: paste the command and compile/runtime flags pls.

anya: repro: `./run_onboard --model=magnet-32k-int4v2 --prompt=tests/long/24k.txt --quant=int4v2 --kv-window=32768 --kv-autoshrink=on --rope_policy=auto`
logs (trim):
`[2026-06-11T04:12:01Z] kv: autoshrink -> new_window=28672 cause=oom; [2026-06-11T04:12:02Z] prefill shard=4 write seq_base=13920 len=1024 fp=0x7f1a2b3c rope_scale=1.0009; [2026-06-11T04:12:02Z] decode read shard=4 seq=13920 fp=0x7f1a2b3b rope_scale=0.9996; token_dup: token[16200]==token[9530]`

carlos: fp LSB changed and rope_scale mismatch. Two suspects: autoshrink rebase producing a negative/non-normalized seq_base, or roperescale recomputed at decode instead of being snapshotted in shard header.

ben: did you try disabling autoshrink or forcing rope_policy=fixed?

anya: yes, turning off autoshrink removes the repro. q4_0 still shows rare drift; int8 no repro.

carlos: quick fix plan: 1) disable autoshrink for int4 canaries; 2) add an assertion in kv writer to reject negative seq_base; 3) snapshot rope_scale into shard metadata at write/merge and prefer header value on replay. Longer term: add regression matrix (int4/q4_0/int8) x (autoshrink on/off) to CI.

ben: I'll open a small PR to add the assert + unit test for prefill->autoshrink->replay. can you file an internal ticket with dumps?

anya: filed: KV-AUTOSHRINK-30555 with repro, traces, and packed-dump. Link: https://redwood.internal/issue/KV-AUTOSHRINK-30555. Also disabled autoshrink on the staging canary and re-ran the sample; drift disappeared. Leaving soak for 8h.

ci-bot: CI job queued: CI/longprefill#30555 (staging)  will post results. :gear:

ben: thanks — I'll pick up the assert PR and add the Rope snapshot change as follow-up.

carlos: I'll add a microtest that simulates autoshrink during prefill and verifies fingerprint equality. Good catch. :thumbsup:
